rv.q: Playwright Benjamin Benne carefully weaves family history, personal dynamics, and a well-loved recipe into a memorable play.
The performances anchor the strong script.
Benne’s writing is poetic, raw, and unapologetically candid, never more so than when Celeste sums up generations of survival
Moreno and Ramos both shine in portraying these internal conflicts and Guevara deserves a special mention as well.
For a drama that can be so grounded in the tactile, with its actresses kneading masa dough in front of us, Fantasma is surprisingly withholding when it comes to key information about its characters.

cn.t: Fantasma earns mostly warm reviews for its heartfelt portrait of a Guatemalan-American family across generations, with critics praising its emotional depth and cultural specificity.
